draft.title: Solving exponential equations
card: To solve an equation with \(x\) in the power, take logarithms of both sides. This brings the power down: \(3^{x} = 20\) becomes \(x \log 3 = \log 20\).
Then divide: \(x = \log 20 \div \log 3 \approx 2.73\). Use the same base on both sides. Use your calculator's \(\log\) button.
Get the power on its own first. For \(2 \times 3^{x} = 40\), divide both sides by 2 to get \(3^{x} = 20\), then take logarithms.
draft.remember: Isolate the power, take logs of both sides, then divide

a.q: Find \(x\) if \(5^{x} = 40\). Round to 2 decimal places.
a.why: Taking logs gives \(x \log 5 = \log 40\), so \(x = \log 40 \div \log 5 \approx 2.29\). Dividing 40 by 5 to get 8 is tempting, but that treats \(5^{x}\) as \(5 \times x\), and it is not.
a.clue: Bring the power down with logs, then divide the two log values.

b.why: Divide both sides by 4 to get \(3^{x} = 25\), so \(x = \log 25 \div \log 3 \approx 2.93\). Taking \(\log 100\) straight away gives 4.19, which skips the step of getting \(3^{x}\) alone.
b.clue: Get \(3^{x}\) on its own before you take logs.

problems.detail: The card ends with an empty bullet line, which will show as a blank dot point. Remove it.

The why says 'Taking log 100 straight away gives 4.19, which skips the step of getting 3^x alone.' Taking logs of both sides first is valid if done properly (log 4 + x log 3 = log 100). The 4.19 comes from ignoring the 4 and computing log 100 ÷ log 3, and the why should say that.

check.summary: Both answers are correct: 2.29 and 2.93. The card has a stray empty bullet, and the why for (b) slightly misdescribes the 4.19 distractor as 'taking log 100 straight away' when the error is ignoring the 4.
